Repeating groups and first normal form

Unit 2 · Week 3 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the normalisation chapter, normalisation-workbook.md, normalisation-answers.md and the normalisation-pack.zip stage datasets. Use fictional data on paper or in a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL setup or student account is required. Keep original copies. Suggested 55-minute timings are flexible. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Repeating groups and first normal form

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the reservation extension of the equipment desk. These are reservation requests, not issued loans. Keep the earlier Loan datasets unchanged. All activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

2. A reservation has its own rules

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

Recall that keys follow requirements. These reservation rules differ from the single-item Loan model. Competing requests can exist. Requested or Confirmed is the exercise status, and separate availability/approval rules must resolve conflicts. Ask students which combination distinguishes one request. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

3. Three maintenance problems

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

An anomaly is a maintenance problem caused by the way facts are stored together. The starter repeats equipment descriptions and category facts inside reservation entries. Do not invent a borrower/date just to register an unused item. The delete example concerns this register’s only stored copy of E03 facts. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

4. A repeating group becomes rows

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher model

Open normalisation-starter.json. Nested JSON is a teaching representation, not inherently an invalid format. Item1/Date1, Item2/Date2 columns create a similar repeating layout. Atomic means one value for the attribute’s purpose: Learner A can remain one label. Flatten all six events without discarding repeated IDs. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

5. Why all three key fields matter

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

This is a four-row extract from the six reservations. The first two need the date to distinguish them, first and third need borrower, first and fourth need item. The rules justify PK (BorrowerID, EquipmentID, ReservationDate). Underline all three components. A sample alone cannot prove a permanent key rule. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

6. Six rows in 1NF

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 1–3 and the 1NF register CSV as a check after an independent attempt. Eight fields: BorrowerID, EquipmentID, ReservationDate, BorrowerLabel, EquipmentDescription, CategoryID, CategoryName, ReservationStatus. There are six rows. Repeating descriptive values can remain in 1NF. Do not confuse one value per field with eliminating all repeated values. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

7. A label with two words

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. BorrowerLabel represents one display label, so Learner A is one value for this purpose. Atomicity depends on the attribute’s meaning and use. Multiple reservation events in one field are the repeating-group problem in this exercise. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

8. A new reservation date

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

The new date creates a distinct request under the three-part key rule. Keep both requests and their own statuses. A duplicate of the exact same borrower/item/date is prohibited. Normalisation does not approve a request or confirm availability. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.
